name: Tool Documentation Enables Zero-Shot Tool-Usage with Large Language Models
venue: arXiv preprint (arXiv:2308.00675); not published at a peer-reviewed venue as of record
authors_affiliation: Cheng-Yu Hsieh (University of Washington), Si-An Chen (National Taiwan University), Chun-Liang Li, Chen-Yu Lee (Google Cloud AI Research), Yasuhisa Fujii (Google Research), Alexander Ratner (University of Washington), Ranjay Krishna (University of Washington), Tomas Pfister (Google Cloud AI Research). Primary affiliations: University of Washington, National Taiwan University, Google Cloud AI Research, Google Research.
code_url: N/A (no official public code repository released by the authors; the LLM-Cloud CLI dataset and prompts are described in the appendix only)
task_domain: tool-use (LLM tool/API planning) across language and vision modalities; multi-modal QA, tabular math reasoning, compositional visual reasoning, image editing, and video tracking
problem_setting: Offline, single-agent, zero-shot/in-context tool-use planning. An LLM planner (primarily ChatGPT/gpt-3.5-turbo, also text-davinci-002) is given a task and a set of available tools/APIs and must produce an executable tool-use plan WITHOUT few-shot demonstrations. No model fine-tuning is performed; tools (including just-released, unseen vision models) are introduced solely by their documentation. The central assumption tested is that tool documentation (per-tool descriptions / docstrings) can replace input-output demonstrations, including in plug-and-play settings where new unseen tools are added at test time.
what_is_retrieved: tool documentation (per-tool descriptions / docstrings: tool functionality descriptions and how to invoke each tool). In the large-tool-set setting (LLM-Cloud CLI with 200 tools) the relevant tool documents are retrieved per question; in the small-tool-set benchmarks the docs for all tools are simply placed in the prompt.
retrieval_grounding: STATIC external corpus: a fixed store of tool documentation (e.g., GCP CLI manuals scraped and renamed, VisProg module docs, original Chameleon tool docs). The store does not grow from the agent's own experience; new tools are added manually by inserting their documentation.
completeness_vs_topk_objective: Mixed. For small tool sets, all tool docs are provided (no ranking needed). For the 200-tool LLM-Cloud CLI, retrieval uses a fixed top-k (top-10 TF-IDF documents) truncated to a length budget; the downstream objective is task completeness, since each question requires at least two commands and is scored by command-line-level F1 measuring recovery of the needed command set, not a single ranking.
cbr_cycle_coverage: N/A (not a case-based reasoning method; no Retrieve/Reuse/Revise/Retain case cycle is implemented)
explicit_cbr_grounding: False. The work does not frame itself as case-based reasoning and does not cite Aamodt & Plaza / Kolodner; it contrasts documentation-based zero-shot tool use against demonstration-based (in-context example) tool use.
retrieval_unit: tool-API / tool documentation document (per-tool description / docstring; for the CLI benchmark, a per-command documentation page)
index_source: Static corpus constructed offline: tool documentation collected from original benchmark tool docs (ScienceQA/Chameleon, TabMWP/Chameleon), author-written module docs for VisProg tools, and scraped+renamed GCP CLI manuals for the LLM-Cloud CLI benchmark. No online/test-time induction; new tool docs are added manually.
index_structure_topology: Flat document store. For the 200-tool LLM-Cloud CLI, a flat TF-IDF index over tool documents; for small tool sets, docs are simply concatenated into the prompt with no special structure.
retriever_type: Sparse lexical: TF-IDF search (used only for the 200-tool LLM-Cloud CLI benchmark, querying with the question to retrieve relevant tool docs). For all other tasks no retriever is used (all tool docs fit in the prompt).
retriever_learning_signal: none (off-the-shelf, unlearned TF-IDF; no training of the retriever)
query_construction: Raw input question used directly as the TF-IDF query to retrieve relevant tool documentation (no decomposition, expansion, or thought-conditioning).
query_granularity: task-level (one query formed from the input question at the start; one-shot retrieval at t=0)
when_to_retrieve: one-shot (retrieve relevant tool docs once before planning, only in the large-tool-set CLI setting; no retrieval for small tool sets)
retrieval_trigger_signal: fixed schedule / driven only by prompt-length constraints: retrieval is triggered when the full set of tool documentation cannot fit in the prompt (200 tools); otherwise all docs are included with no trigger.
reranking: None. A single TF-IDF top-10 retrieval is used with no reranking stage.
retrieved_context_refinement: Length truncation/compression only: retrieved documents are truncated to a maximum of ~600 words to fit the prompt budget; no rerank, distillation, or distractor filtering. The authors deliberately keep unrelated content (terms, hyperlinks) to test robustness.
tool_document_engineering: Mostly raw docstrings/manuals: original tool docs are reused (ScienceQA/TabMWP via Chameleon); for VisProg modules the authors write docs containing the module functionality description plus the function signature; for LLM-Cloud CLI, GCP manuals are scraped with BeautifulSoup, HTML tags removed and commands renamed, but content is deliberately NOT curated/engineered (unrelated terms/hyperlinks kept) to assess robustness.
index_content_separation: Partial: in the 200-tool CLI setting, a lightweight TF-IDF index over docs selects which tool documents to load into the prompt, separating selection from the full documentation content; for small tool sets there is no separation.
dynamic_index_and_protocol: Static tool index (no live synchronization, no CRUD auto-sync). Integration is via prompt-based plan generation; for vision tasks tools are invoked through the VisProg program-execution framework, and for CLI via generated command-line strings. No RapidAPI/MCP/function-calling protocol.
tool_dependency_awareness: Limited/implicit. Retrieval does not explicitly model inter-tool dependencies; however the LLM planner, by reading docs, can infer multi-step pipelines (e.g., GroundingDINO + SAM for segmentation feeding XMem for tracking, or a hidden 'create a topic before sending messages' step), so dependency handling is emergent from the planner rather than encoded in the index.
how_retrieved_used: prompt augmentation: retrieved/provided tool documentation is inserted into the LLM prompt, and the LLM zero-shot generates a tool-use plan (a sequence of tool calls / a VisProg program / CLI commands) by reading the docs. No fine-tuning; docs guide the model's internal planning and reasoning.
planning_integration: retrieve-then-plan / one-shot exemplar-free plan time: documentation is provided up front and the LLM produces a complete tool-use plan in a single zero-shot pass (no per-step interleaved retrieval, no tree search). For vision tasks the plan is a VisProg program executed afterwards.
reasoning_search_interleaving_granularit: per-answer (the LLM generates the full multi-tool plan in one shot from the provided documentation; retrieval is not interleaved per reasoning step)
adaptation_mechanism: N/A (no case adaptation; documentation is used verbatim as prompt context and the LLM directly generates plans)
retrieved_item_representation: raw free-text tool documentation (natural-language tool descriptions plus function signatures / CLI manuals) injected into the prompt
abstraction_level_of_retrieved_unit: tool-level descriptive documentation (a hint/manual describing each individual tool's functionality and invocation), not raw trajectories or distilled strategies; it is per-tool capability description rather than task-level demonstration
noise_robustness_mechanism: Tested-not-engineered: the authors intentionally do NOT curate documentation (keeping unrelated terms/hyperlinks, varying doc length) to assess the LLM's robustness to realistic/noisy docs; they report a length ablation showing degradation past ~600 words. No explicit retriever-aware training or relevance evaluator is used.
memory_type: none (no episodic, skill-library, or procedural memory that the system writes to; only a static, manually-maintained documentation store)
write_back: False. The system does not store new experiences/cases/skills; the tool documentation store is static and only manually extended with new tools' docs.
online_growth: No. The retrievable store does not grow from deployment experience; new tools are added by humans inserting their documentation (plug-and-play), not by the agent writing back.
failure_experience_usage: N/A (no experience/memory storage, so no use of failed or successful trajectories)
memory_evolution_update: N/A (no stored memory entries; the static doc store is not mutated by the system)
retrieval_as_learned_policy: No. Retrieval (where used) is a fixed off-the-shelf TF-IDF top-k, not a learned/RL-optimized policy.
cross_agent_or_cross_framework_sharing: No. Single-agent, single-framework use; no cross-agent or cross-framework memory/experience sharing. (Tool docs themselves are shareable artifacts, but there is no shared experience memory.)
benchmarks: ScienceQA; TabMWP; NLVRv2; LLM-Cloud CLI (newly collected, 200 commands renamed from GCP CLI, 50 questions); image editing and video tracking with VisProg expanded by GroundingDINO + Segment Anything (SAM) + XMem (qualitative, re-inventing Grounded-SAM and Track Anything).
benchmark_family: Tool-use / multi-modal tool planning. ScienceQA = multi-modal QA; TabMWP = tabular math reasoning; NLVRv2 = compositional visual reasoning (VisProg); LLM-Cloud CLI = realistic large tool-set API/CLI tool-use (new benchmark, GCP-derived); image editing + video tracking = vision tool pipelines.
baselines: Few-shot demonstration prompting (varying number of demos, with and without docs); demos+docs combinations. Task-specific: ScienceQA - CoT, Chameleon (few-shot) and finetuned models (e.g., UnifiedQA, others on the SQA training set); TabMWP - UnifiedQA, TAPEX (finetuned), Chain-of-Thought (CoT), Program-of-Thoughts (PoT), Chameleon (few-shot); NLVRv2 - ViLT-NLVR (finetuned), VisProg (few-shot, varying demos); LLM-Cloud CLI - zero-shot LLM, few-shot demos without docs, and docs+demos, on text-davinci-002 and gpt-3.5-turbo.
key_metrics: Accuracy (ScienceQA, TabMWP, NLVRv2); command-line-level F1 averaged over 50 examples (LLM-Cloud CLI); qualitative success of generated pipelines (image editing, video tracking).
headline_result: Zero-shot tool-documentation prompting matches few-shot performance on existing benchmarks and far outperforms demonstrations on the 200-tool LLM-Cloud CLI: with gpt-3.5-turbo, 0-shot with docs reaches F1 0.45 vs 0.13 zero-shot no-doc and best few-shot no-doc F1 0.19; with text-davinci-002, 0-shot with docs F1 0.37 vs 0.02 zero-shot no-doc and best few-shot no-doc 0.05. On benchmarks, 0-shot with docs achieves 79.91 (ScienceQA), 92.69 (TabMWP), and 63.40 (NLVRv2, vs 0.00 without docs), competitive with or better than CoT/PoT few-shot and some finetuned models.
ablations: (1) Number of demonstrations: stripping demos away barely changes accuracy when docs are present (0-shot+docs on par with 16-shot on TabMWP, 12-shot on NLVRv2, and better than 10-shot on ScienceQA), while without docs performance drops sharply and shows high variance to which demos are chosen (e.g., 2-shot std up to 16.1 points on NLVRv2). (2) Docs vs docs+demos: adding demos to docs does not help and can slightly hurt (text-davinci-002 docs-only 0.37 vs docs+demos avg 0.35; gpt-3.5-turbo docs-only 0.45 vs 0.44/0.44/0.42), showing demos are redundant given docs. (3) Documentation quality/length: truncating docs to first n words; performance degrades after document length exceeds ~600 words, attributed to long-context comprehension limits. (4) Different LLM planners (text-davinci-002 vs gpt-3.5-turbo) on LLM-Cloud CLI confirm docs >> demos at large tool counts.
evaluation_decoupling: No. Retrieval quality (the TF-IDF doc retrieval) is not evaluated with intrinsic metrics (Recall@k/nDCG); only end-to-end task metrics (accuracy / command-line F1) are reported.
process_vs_outcome_metrics: Primarily outcome metrics (final accuracy / F1). Some process-level insight via command-line-level F1 (which credits partial recovery of the needed commands/flags) and qualitative inspection of generated plans/pipelines, but no formal reasoning-faithfulness or step-wise planning metric.
cost_efficiency_tradeoff: Efficiency framed as avoiding combinatorial demo-selection cost and human curation: documentation is 'organically available' and zero-shot, eliminating few-shot demo curation and the combinatorial search over which/how-many demos to include as tool counts scale. Prompt-length is the binding cost: docs are truncated (~600 words/tool; top-10 docs in the 200-tool setting) and performance degrades past ~600 words. No explicit latency/API-cost numbers reported.
context_budget_and_selection_count: For the 200-tool LLM-Cloud CLI: fixed top-10 TF-IDF documents, each truncated to a maximum of ~600 words to fit the prompt (token count varies by tokenizer, typically >600). For small tool sets: all tool docs included (no k selection). Documentation-length ablation shows ~600 words is roughly the effective budget before long-context degradation.
benchmark_construction_and_size: LLM-Cloud CLI: newly collected; 200 command-line tools renamed from the Google Cloud Platform (GCP) CLI to be unseen to LLMs while preserving semantics (e.g., 'gcloud compute create NAME' -> 'llmvm compute make NAME'); 50 questions, each requiring at least two commands; docs scraped from real GCP manuals via BeautifulSoup with HTML removed and renaming applied, deliberately not over-curated. Answer verifiability via command-line-level F1 against reference commands. Best system (gpt-3.5-turbo, 0-shot with docs) reaches F1 0.45, signaling the benchmark is far from saturated.
builds_on: VisProg (Gupta & Kembhavi) and Chameleon (Lu et al.) tool-use frameworks (tool sets reused); in-context learning / few-shot prompting (Brown et al.); DocPrompting (Zhou et al., retrieving docs for code generation) as the closest documentation-based predecessor; uses GroundingDINO, Segment Anything (SAM), XMem, and Stable Diffusion as plug-in tools.
contrasts_with: Demonstration/few-shot-based tool-use methods (VisProg, Chameleon, MM-REACT, HuggingGPT, ART, Visual ChatGPT/TaskMatrix); instruction-tuning-on-synthetic-tool-data approaches (Gorilla, ToolLLM/ToolBench-style works that finetune LLaMA/OPT on GPT-4-generated tool-use data); ViperGPT (concurrent, function implementations/specs as docs for visual programming); AutoGPT (anecdotal doc reading). The paper argues documentation alone, zero-shot, suffices and avoids demo-selection and finetuning costs.
lineage: Group E (tool-use). An early (Aug 2023) position/empirical work establishing that tool documentation (static external doc grounding) can substitute for few-shot demonstrations for zero-shot tool/API usage, including unseen tools; a conceptual predecessor to later tool-retrieval and tool-documentation-engineering lines (e.g., Gorilla, ToolBench/ToolLLM, and doc-augmented tool-retrieval works).
